title: Build your own agent harness like DeepSeek's
topic: How the DeepSeek Harness agent harness is built, from first principles
summary: Starting from what a language model is, you learn every part of an agent harness and how the open-source DeepSeek Harness builds it, from its source code. Module by module you write mini-dsh in TypeScript: a plugin kernel, an event log, a DeepSeek adapter, safe tools, a sandbox, context management, subagents and an SDK.

concepts.name: Language model
concepts.summary: A language model writes text by predicting one likely next piece at a time.

concepts.name: Tokens
concepts.summary: Models read and write text as numbered chunks called tokens.

concepts.name: The context window
concepts.summary: A model can only consider a fixed number of tokens in one request.

concepts.name: A model API call
concepts.summary: Your program sends a JSON request to a hosted model and reads the reply.

concepts.name: Message roles
concepts.summary: A chat request is a list of messages labelled system, user or assistant.

concepts.name: A stateless model
concepts.summary: The model remembers nothing between requests, so the program sends the history every time.

concepts.name: Streaming
concepts.summary: A reply can come as a stream of small events, and it ends with a reason the model stopped.

concepts.name: Tool schema
concepts.summary: Each function is described by a name, a description and a JSON Schema for its arguments.

concepts.name: Tool call
concepts.summary: Instead of text, the model can reply with a structured request to run one function.

concepts.name: Tool result
concepts.summary: The program runs the function and sends the outcome back, matched by a call id.

concepts.name: The agent loop
concepts.summary: A program repeats model request, function run and result until the model answers in text.

concepts.name: Turn
concepts.summary: A turn answers the user once; each model request inside it is a step, and a limit caps the steps.

concepts.name: Tool error result
concepts.summary: A failed function still returns a result, marked as an error, so the model can try again.

concepts.name: The first agent
concepts.summary: All the pieces so far, joined into one working agent of about sixty lines.

concepts.name: Append-only log
concepts.summary: Writing every fact in order and never editing an old fact.

concepts.name: Session event
concepts.summary: Each fact has a type, a sequence number, a time and its data.

concepts.name: Model-visible means logged
concepts.summary: Anything the model sees must first be written to the record, so any request can be rebuilt.

concepts.name: Derived history
concepts.summary: The messages sent to the model are made by reading the record from the start.

concepts.name: The logged system prompt
concepts.summary: The system prompt is written to the record as a message, not passed beside it.

concepts.name: JSONL storage
concepts.summary: The record is saved as a file with one JSON event per line, written before each model call.

concepts.name: Session resume
concepts.summary: Reading the file back and closing any turn that was cut off.

concepts.name: Orphaned tool call
concepts.summary: When a call has no result, the program writes a made-up error result so the history stays valid.

concepts.name: Format versions
concepts.summary: Each layout version has its own file name, and small steps convert one version to the next.

concepts.name: Stream chunk
concepts.summary: A shared list of piece types: block start, text, reasoning, tool arguments, block end, usage, finish.

concepts.name: Block assembler
concepts.summary: A small function folds the pieces of a stream into complete text and tool-call blocks.

concepts.name: Adapter seam
concepts.summary: Every provider sits behind one stream method, so the loop never knows which one it talks to.

concepts.name: The DeepSeek wire
concepts.summary: DeepSeek accepts a subset of the Anthropic Messages format, which the adapter writes and reads.

concepts.name: Reasoning block
concepts.summary: DeepSeek streams thinking with a signature, and the harness sends it back unchanged on later requests.

concepts.name: Prefix caching
concepts.summary: The provider reuses work when a request begins with the same bytes, so the harness only appends.

concepts.name: Retry with backoff
concepts.summary: A failed request is retried after a growing wait, and each retry is written to the record.

concepts.name: Cancellation
concepts.summary: An abort signal stops the stream; what arrived is kept and the turn ends with a reason.

concepts.name: Context
concepts.summary: Every plugin receives a context object, and child contexts inherit from their parent.

concepts.name: Plugin lifecycle
concepts.summary: A mounted plugin moves from pending to active to disposed.

concepts.name: Disposer
concepts.summary: Every registration returns a function that undoes it, run in reverse order when the plugin stops.

concepts.name: Service
concepts.summary: A plugin names the services it needs and stays pending until they exist.

concepts.name: Events
concepts.summary: Events can be sent to all listeners at once, in order, or until one answers.

concepts.name: Waterfall hook
concepts.summary: Each listener gets a next function; skipping it stops the chain.

concepts.name: Isolate realm
concepts.summary: A context can replace one service name for everything below it, without changing its parent.

concepts.name: Agent scope
concepts.summary: A tag on a child context makes its listeners and tools apply only to one agent.

concepts.name: Config rows
concepts.summary: The plugin tree is a list of rows, and patches replace or insert rows by id.

concepts.name: Profile
concepts.summary: A profile stacks bundles of rows in order; reloading disposes and mounts again.

concepts.name: defineTool
concepts.summary: A tool definition converts its parameters to a schema, checks the arguments and returns one value.

concepts.name: Tool registry
concepts.summary: Tools register on a shared service and disappear when their plugin stops.

concepts.name: Batch scheduling
concepts.summary: Calls run in parallel only when each one says it is safe; all others run alone.

concepts.name: Pre-execute decision
concepts.summary: A waterfall of policies decides allow, deny or ask, and guards can only deny.

concepts.name: Approval
concepts.summary: An ask goes to a person; with nobody to answer, the call is denied.

concepts.name: Around-execute wrapper
concepts.summary: A wrapper around the tool body adds timeouts, retries and timing.

concepts.name: Post-execute
concepts.summary: After a tool runs, listeners can replace the result, block it or add context.

concepts.name: Output spill
concepts.summary: A result that is too large is saved to a file, and the model sees its start, end and the file name.

concepts.name: File tools
concepts.summary: Read, write and edit tools, and why an edit checks that the file did not change.

concepts.name: Shell tool
concepts.summary: A bash tool starts a process with a clean environment and returns its output.

concepts.name: Sandbox modes
concepts.summary: A mode names where commands may write, and the workspace folders are the write roots.

concepts.name: Sandbox backend
concepts.summary: Seatbelt on macOS and bwrap on Linux enforce the mode, and a mode that cannot be enforced stops the call.

concepts.name: Escalation
concepts.summary: After a denial the model may retry the same call once with a justification for a person to approve.

concepts.name: Permission presets
concepts.summary: Named presets join a sandbox mode with an approval policy for one session.

concepts.name: Prompt sections
concepts.summary: Plugins add ordered sections, and the harness renders them into one system prompt.

concepts.name: Runtime context
concepts.summary: A pre-step hook adds facts such as the time as user messages that are logged.

concepts.name: Project instructions
concepts.summary: The harness reads AGENTS.md and adds it again after a tool changes it.

concepts.name: Token meter
concepts.summary: An estimate of the request's tokens, checked against a threshold below the context window.

concepts.name: Safe cut
concepts.summary: Walk back from the newest message and never split a tool call from its result.

concepts.name: Surface replacement
concepts.summary: A summary replaces a range in the model's view while the record keeps every fact.

concepts.name: Overflow recovery
concepts.summary: When the provider rejects a request as too large, the harness summarises and retries the step.

concepts.name: MCP client
concepts.summary: The Model Context Protocol lets the harness list and call tools that another program offers.

concepts.name: MCP tools
concepts.summary: Each server tool is registered under a prefixed name, so every policy applies to it.

concepts.name: Skills
concepts.summary: A short catalog sits in the prompt, and one tool loads a skill's full text on request.

concepts.name: Programmatic tool calling
concepts.summary: One run_code tool replaces the others, and the model writes a program that calls them.

concepts.name: Code channel
concepts.summary: A generated typed SDK in the prompt, and a JSON-lines channel back to the harness process.

concepts.name: Sub-call limits
concepts.summary: Each call from the program goes through the same policies, with rate and parallel limits.

concepts.name: Agent inbox
concepts.summary: Messages wait in an inbox; steer joins the next step, followup the next turn.

concepts.name: Agent registry
concepts.summary: A service creates, finds and resumes agents, each with its own session.

concepts.name: Subagent
concepts.summary: A tool starts a child agent with a fresh session, up to a depth limit.

concepts.name: Child isolation
concepts.summary: A child gets a restricted tool list and no approval prompts, and its policy is logged.

concepts.name: Subagent result
concepts.summary: The child's last answer returns to the parent as a message in the parent's inbox.

concepts.name: Agent team
concepts.summary: A durable task board where each task has one owner, changed with compare-and-set.

concepts.name: Workflow
concepts.summary: The model writes a script that starts agents in parallel and in steps.

concepts.name: Todo list
concepts.summary: One tool replaces the whole list each time, and the record keeps every version.

concepts.name: Plan mode
concepts.summary: A mode adds planning guidance before each step, and a person approves the plan.

concepts.name: Goal driver
concepts.summary: When the agent goes idle, a driver sends a follow-up prompt until the goal is done or a cap is hit.

concepts.name: Background job
concepts.summary: A job has an id and an output buffer, and a notice tells the session when it ends.

concepts.name: Schedule
concepts.summary: A timer sends a prompt to a session on a cron pattern, and sends only the latest missed run.

concepts.name: Live event stream
concepts.summary: Session events and live stream frames let a screen follow the agent as it works.

concepts.name: Headless runner
concepts.summary: A runner takes one prompt, prints the answer and exits with a status code.

concepts.name: JSON-RPC over stdio
concepts.summary: Requests and notifications as JSON lines over a child process's input and output.

concepts.name: Agent Client Protocol
concepts.summary: ACP lets an editor create sessions and send prompts over the same kind of stream.

concepts.name: Web gateway
concepts.summary: HTTP routes and generated RPC stubs let a web page drive the agent.

concepts.name: Mock adapter
concepts.summary: An adapter that plays back scripted streams, so tests run without a real model.

concepts.name: Fault server
concepts.summary: A local HTTP server that speaks the provider's format and injects errors and stalls.

concepts.name: Replay
concepts.summary: Model streams saved in a session file are played back to test a change.

concepts.name: Outcome checks
concepts.summary: Tests check the files and the record the agent left, not what the agent says it did.

concepts.name: The whole harness
concepts.summary: How every part joins into mini-dsh, traced through one request.
